standard_prerequisites.name: Function extensionality
standard_prerequisites.statement: A homotopy between two functions may be turned into an equality of functions.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is applied twice, at source line 338 for the first half and at source lines 344-345 for the second.

standard_prerequisites.name: Mere proposition and set
standard_prerequisites.statement: A type is a mere proposition when all its identity types are contractible and a set when all its identity types are mere propositions; every mere proposition is a set.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the level information that either witness supplies at source lines 340-341 and 343-344.

standard_prerequisites.name: 1-type
standard_prerequisites.statement: A type is a 1-type when all its identity types are sets.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the level that either witness of sethood supplies at source line 344.

core_obligations: For f and g in the type of proofs that A is a mere proposition, apply function extensionality to reduce f = g to the pointwise statement that f(x,y) = g(x,y) for all x and y in A (source line 338).

Observe that f(x,y) and g(x,y) are both paths in A between the same endpoints, and that either witness already makes A a mere proposition, hence a set by the preceding result, so those two paths are equal (source lines 340-341).
For f and g in the type of proofs that A is a set, read the two witnesses as functions sending a, b, p and q to a proof that p = q, and compare them pointwise in the same way (source lines 342-344).
Conclude f = g in both cases by function extensionality (source lines 338 and 344-345).

proof_roadmap.step: First half: extensionality reduces the comparison of two mere-proposition witnesses to a comparison of paths, closed by sethood.
Second half: the same reduction one level up, where the witnesses are proofs that parallel paths are equal.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled lemma thm:isprop-isprop at source lines 334-336: for every type A the types of proofs that A is a mere proposition and that A is a set are mere propositions. The author's proof (source lines 337-346) has to extract level information from a witness that is only available hypothetically, and it does so twice at different levels. To compare two mere-proposition witnesses it applies function extensionality and then notices that the two values f(x,y) and g(x,y) are paths in A between the same endpoints, equal only because either witness already makes A a mere proposition, hence a set by the preceding result (source lines 338-341). The second half repeats the same manoeuvre for witnesses of sethood, which are functions of four arguments landing in an identity type (source lines 342-345). The statement does not show that equality of the two witnesses is obtained by first turning one of them into a level bound for A.
